hints: Look closely at what W, X and Y are pointing to in the micrograph. W shows stacked membranes with starch grains, X is the layer between the two cells, Y is the boundary of the cell.
Remember the golden test for eukaryotic cells: membrane-bound organelles and a true nucleus. Ask yourself which of W, X and Y are also found in prokaryotic cells.
walkthrough:
**Identify the three labels**

Look at the structures first. W is a chloroplast with its internal thylakoid membranes. X is the plant cell wall between the two cells. Y is the cell surface (plasma) membrane at the edge of the cell.

**Recall what proves a cell is eukaryotic**

Eukaryotic cells have a true nucleus enclosed by a nuclear envelope and membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria, chloroplasts, Golgi body and rough endoplasmic reticulum. Prokaryotic cells lack all of these.

**Check which labels are unique to eukaryotes**

Both prokaryotes and eukaryotes have a cell surface membrane (Y) and many have a cell wall (X), so X and Y cannot prove the cell is eukaryotic. Only W, a membrane-bound chloroplast, is found exclusively in eukaryotes, so W only is the answer.

options.A: Incorrect, because X (cell wall) and Y (cell surface membrane) are also found in prokaryotic cells, so they do not prove the cell is eukaryotic.
options.B: Incorrect, because X is a cell wall which is present in many prokaryotes as well as in plants, so it is not a eukaryotic-only feature.
options.C: Correct, because W is a chloroplast, a membrane-bound organelle. Membrane-bound organelles are only found in eukaryotic cells.
options.D: Incorrect, because X is the cell wall, which does not identify a cell as eukaryotic since prokaryotes can also have cell walls.
